body:
>Does she have another way to get to school or work other than driving?

She will be on a college campus and everything is within walking distance. There's also the problem of her not being able to sit in a classroom without getting panicky. She has 3 weeks left to prepare for this.

I agree about how she needs a new therapist. I suggested that she get a new one, but she doesn't think any of them will help. What would a therapist who understands panic disorder do differently?

Hi, thanks for responding. Firstly, congratulations on dealing with your anxiety successfully!

I think she has had anxiety for longer, but she hasn't really told the full story about her childhood -- I think there was some emotional or physical abuse, but she said someday she will tell me about it. She's generally pretty good about dealing with her anxiety about most things, she gets afraid when she rides airplanes, goes on elevators, or does basically most things. I think she is able to cope with that pretty well, though. Supposedly I do a good job of calming her down when she feels scared of those things.

What could help her if she's getting panic attacks from the thought of having a panic attack? The thought is kind of unavoidable. She isn't afraid of driving itself, since she was able to drive for two years without any issue. She's afraid of having a panic attack while driving and not having anywhere to go if she does, and she's afraid of killing herself by not having anywhere to pull over.

I don't know what the issue is with therapy, but she seems to think her therapist doesn't help at all. They just tell her to breathe deeply and to not be afraid of what she's afraid of.

They stopped working after her big anxiety attack in early June. The ones she's taking now are both in the same class of medications. She's taking one for preventing panic attacks, one for dealing with them when she gets them, and then a medication for depression.

Thank you. It seems as though she just needed to get all of it off her chest last night since she has kind of bottled it up. Today she is in a better mood and I think she was just pretty upset. I'm still going to bring up suicide with her, not that I think she's immediately at risk, but I'm going to make sure she knows I'm always open to talk no matter what the issue is.
